A fruit that shares a name with a color is orange.

Postmodernism is a broad movement that developed in the mid- to late-20th century across diverse fields, including literature, architecture, art, and philosophy. In relation to literature, postmodernism is characterized by a self-consciousness about narrative conventions, a skepticism toward grand narratives or absolute truths, and a blending of high and low culture. Postmodern literary works often employ techniques such as fragmentation, non-linear timelines, unreliable narrators, metafiction (where the text draws attention to its own artificiality), and intertextuality (referencing other texts). Authors associated with postmodernism include Thomas Pynchon, Don DeLillo, Kurt Vonnegut, and Jorge Luis Borges. The movement often challenges the idea of objective reality and emphasizes the role of the reader in constructing meaning.
